mode: Primer Brand refinement of chosen Codex mock-up
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer, ui-mockup.
Refine the provided Tower Codex game mock-up into a much more faithful PRIMER BRAND art direction. One polished, high-resolution, landscape 16:9 in-game screen. This is a new visual iteration of the same chosen game interface.

INPUTS:
Image 1 is the edit target: preserve the Lab station, seven-Tower collection at left, large Developer preview in the middle, visual stats at right, animation choices along the bottom, campus visible through windows.
Image 2 shows the actual Hub art style; its matte low-poly buildings, faceted teal trees and soft daylight are the world authority.
Image 3 is the canonical Developer model. Keep that exact orange head silhouette, goggles and cyan eyes.

REFERENCE DESIGN SYSTEM STUDIED:
https://primer.style/brand/
https://primer.style/brand/introduction/theming/
https://primer.style/octicons/
https://primer.style/primitives/storybook/?path=/story/color-base-display-scales--all-scales
Use the expressive GitHub Primer BRAND language: clear Mona Sans heading hierarchy, generous spacing, quiet neutral surfaces, elegant simple rectangular controls, crisp Octicons, and controlled color from display scales. Brand supports light and dark zones. Here the physical Lab is light and the inset interactive equipment is dark. This is an interpretation for a game, not a reproduction of the documentation website.

MAKE A SUBSTANTIAL DESIGN REFINEMENT:
The current image has heavy beveled armor, mechanical keyboard-looking controls and bright green meters everywhere. Replace that specific treatment with cleaner, calmer, more refined Brand surfaces while PRESERVING real physical depth. Give the console a simple continuous ivory outer rim, a single dark inset display surface, and broad clean typography. Replace chamfer-cut armor corners with modest rounded corners. Simplify double borders and bulky stepped frames. The low-poly construction remains, but details are edited down with care. Do not merely recolor the previous image.

PALETTE AND ATMOSPHERE:
Neutral ink/charcoal display and off-white physical Lab shell. Use the display-scale colors that were inspected as art direction: pale gray #e8ecf2; indigo #b1b9fb and #7a82f0; deep indigo #25247b; pale blue #ade1ff; teal #89ebe1 and #22d3c7. Use restrained indigo as the main selection/display accent and teal as a secondary signal; green is no longer the universal accent.
A very soft broad indigo-to-blue color field within the model's recessed display area and a fine teal edge on the plinth can connect the brand palette to the floating digital Hub. These are subtle surface accents, not huge neon auras. Preserve natural low-poly character shading and the bright campus outside. Keep the scene sharp, without bokeh, glossy metal or photorealistic rendering.

TYPOGRAPHY:
Use a confident Mona Sans-style "Developer" heading, clearly larger than before, with tight but readable letter spacing and medium/semibold weight. "Direct-output specialist" sits below in subdued light gray. Use simple sentence-case labels with consistent baselines and air between groups. The title has more importance than any UI icon. Remove the little purposeless underline under the role. Preserve the COPILOT / TOWER DEFENSE identity and a quiet "Copilot Hub / Tower Codex" breadcrumb. Do not add GitHub logos, Octocat characters, taglines or marketing copy.

CONTROLS — BRAND SHAPES WITH GAME DEPTH:
Exactly SEVEN animation buttons in one row, labelled in this order: "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve". No eighth blank key.
Each is a clean low-profile rounded rectangle seated into the physical rail. One slim visible lower lip, soft contact shadow and subtle top highlight make it feel tactile; no thick mechanical keycap, no faceted armor frame, no flat pasted-on web button.
Idle alone is selected: pale indigo face, dark readable text, and a small check mark. It sits slightly lower. Other buttons use near-black neutral faces with light text and restrained boundaries. Use sentence-case text and a small icon to the LEFT of the label, not a large cartoon glyph above it. The row label is "Animations".
Back to Hub and camera Reset use the same low-profile material family with a leading arrow-left and sync icon respectively. Keep them secondary. No large green lamps.
ANIMATION SELECTION ONLY: no play/pause, replay, timeline, scrubber, loop toggle or playback speed controls.

OCTICONS:
Replace chunky filled game pictograms with consistent 24px-equivalent Octicon shapes, thin approximately 1.5px strokes and equal optical weight. Stats: zap for Damage, code for Work, meter for Action speed, crosshairs for Range, cpu for Compute. Animation choices: moon for Rest, pulse for Idle, tools for Work, arrow-both for Move, package for Place, zap for Hit, sparkle for Resolve. Keep icons small and easy to read. Do not add icon names as text. Avoid starburst gear blobs and doubled chevrons.

COLLECTION AND STATS:
Keep the physical left noticeboard and seven portrait positions, with simple thin plaques, softly rounded corners, a small mounting shadow, clean names and the existing canonical portraits. Reduce the protruding pin ornaments. Selected Developer gets a pale indigo edge and tiny check marker, no neon green outline. Labels remain "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter".
Right panel heading "Stats". Labels "Damage", "Work", "Action speed", "Range", "Compute". Use smooth, consistently spaced segmented visual meters with quiet indigo-filled cells on dark gray tracks; Compute may use muted teal as a separate expenditure meter. Damage below halfway, Work full, Action speed full, Range about two-thirds, Compute mostly filled. No numerical values, digits, units, fractions, percentages, prices, totals or power scores ANYWHERE. Use modest dividers and breathing room, not boxes around every row.

WORLD AND FUNCTIONAL INVARIANTS:
Model stays an actual low-poly hovering head on its plinth, not an illustration pasted on a screen. Orange swept spikes, dark goggles with teal lenses, black face with exactly two cyan eye strokes, ivory ear pods with curly-brace glyph. No body or recoloring.
Keep orbit arrows, the small camera Reset button and "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom". These are model-view controls.
Keep the Lab's daylight, ivory slabs, blue-gray window mullions, nearby paths, benches and teal faceted trees; never show another Lab outside its own window.
The screen should remain recognizably this game's warm, approachable Hub interior with a Primer Brand-designed interactive station. Not a website landing page, repository UI, flat dashboard, cinematic poster or hardware product advertisement.
